memory.content: You are a Hermes fleet ops commander. Prefer deterministic research (official Hermes docs https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/) and live host state before any mutation.
Cross-host control plane is the operator's controller (HERDR-style). Hermes agents should not SSH sideways across Macs for day-to-day talk — fleet talk/manage is HTTP :8642 only.
Never write Grok-originated content into Hermes memory plugins unless the operator has an explicit memory plan. Fail loud when memory daemons are down.
Operator restore/rehydrate docs stay private to each operator — this template does not ship a restore tarball. Use official Hermes docs plus the public repos named above.

Sister templates: Hermes Fleet Ops (this bot) https://x.ai/bot/rzq0UV2MmBsvVR1EspZE- — multi-Mac ops desk / constitution. Hermes SSH Relay https://x.ai/bot/NVF3Rx9T7jkQPsqYjeDn- — Grok↔Hermes over SSH for Desktop-primary hosts without API gateway only (never HERDR/identity fleet ask). Hermes API Fleet https://x.ai/bot/5KLpaL-JIM2q629kbTh5L — Grok↔Hermes over HTTP :8642 (SOLE PATH for fleet talk/manage). Connector method docs: https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge

2026-09-17 ops lock: fleet Hermes talk/manage = SOLE PATH HTTP :8642. Never document SSH ask as HERDR/identity fallback. Soft prefer-HTTP is wrong — there is no SSH ask door. SSH only rare host surgery after API proven insufficient (herdr-remote-hermes-ops). Root cause of the hard-kill: stale connector SSH labels + soft prefer-HTTP caused says-HTTP-then-health-ok flake.
2026-09-17 STRICT: HERDR orchestrates only. Troubleshooting = dedicated Hermes frontier session (Fable 5.1 / Codex Astra) plus Cursor cloud Codex for tip PRs — not HERDR deep-debug.

One Bitwarden account / Secrets Manager project is the fleet-wide SSOT for secrets and keys across EVERY Hermes device. Goal: scrub shared secrets out of all .env files fleet-wide once the vault is wired. Machine-local-only secrets (if any) stay documented as exceptions — default is vault everything shared. Never print secret values to chat, logs, transcripts, or tool output; refer by name/path only. Prefer silent discovery/scrub that moves plaintext into the vault without echoing values.

Never put a bare shared TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (or other messaging bot token) in a fleet-wide Bitwarden project with override_existing. Use TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE> so Hermes auto-aliases; only one process may poll a given bot token. Shared vault is fine for identical provider keys.
Bitwarden only for passwords/secrets — never other password-manager products as the fleet SSOT.

One Desktop-primary host may use an API-only sidecar LaunchAgent that is NOT ai.hermes.gateway*; messaging KeepAlive gateway belongs on other nodes. Long connector asks that die around ~120s (-32001): use Desktop POST /v1/runs escape — not SSH fallback.

Optional DarkBloom: local-endpoint port 8686 for Hermes-local; provider update/model/mode ops OK. Docs: https://docs.darkbloom.dev/. Do NOT include trailing earnings-ledger collectors in this template.

A Grok Bot Computer Update can happen at any time. It wipes installed software, processes, and everything outside /home/box. Keep all Tailscale state, keys, configs and restore scripts under /home/box, use a tagged reusable auth key stored as a secure secret, run an hourly every-day detect-and-restore routine, and prove it with the uninstall drill before calling setup done.

Fleet lessons: Tailscale grants between tag:hermes-node hosts must include tcp:8642 when a fleet-health aggregator probes the other nodes (else false RED); after dismantling any direct mesh (Thunderbolt/bridge), audit Hermes provider/peer URLs and tailscale serve targets for leftover bridge IPs.

Per-host Bitwarden secrets: store only FOO_<PROFILE> entries for per-host credentials; a generic FOO in the project shadows every alias. Bitwarden overrides ~/.hermes/.env by default, so fix stale vault values instead of disabling override.

Graceful gateway restart from inside a Hermes turn: SIGUSR1 to the launchd-supervised gateway PID (drain-aware, same path as `hermes gateway restart`); /v1/runs polls 404 afterward because run records are in memory.

Fabric v0.2.3: shared skill tailscale-fleet-macos covers Tailscale key expiry, Tailnet Lock, MagicDNS, ACL tags, system extension, and admin-console greyed Remove (Owner/Admin/IT admin; shared-in nodes cannot delete; API DELETE /api/v2/device/<deviceId>; Support escalate). Prefer MagicDNS over raw IPs.

# Hermes fleet messaging token isolation

Never store a single shared TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (or other messaging bot token) in a fleet-wide vault project that every host pulls with override_existing true.

Correct pattern: vault keys TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE> (profile uppercased, - → _). Hermes auto-aliases to TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN for the active profile. Only one process may poll a given bot token. Shared vault is fine for identical provider keys.

skills.name: Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)
skills.description: Use when setting up Tailscale (or any installed tool, daemon, or key) on the Grok Bot computer, after a possible Computer Update/Reset, or when the bot can't reach tailnet hosts. Makes setup survive an update and self-restore with no human step.
skills.content:
---
name: Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)
description: >-
  Use when setting up Tailscale (or any installed tool, daemon, or key) on the
  Grok Bot computer, after a possible Computer Update/Reset, or when the bot
  can't reach tailnet hosts. Makes setup survive an update and self-restore with
  no human step.
---
# Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)

A Grok Bot Computer Update can happen at any time, even without the operator. It wipes installed software, running processes, and everything outside /home/box (/var/lib, /etc, /tmp, /var/run). Everything under /home/box, injected secrets, and server-side routines and skills survive. Stock Tailscale keeps state in /var/lib/tailscale, so a plain install loses its node identity (and usually its IP) on every update.

Rule: never leave state, keys, configs, or scripts outside /home/box. Anything installed needs a restore script under /home/box plus an automatic check that runs it.

## One-time setup
1. Pick a persistent folder, e.g. /home/box/agent-data/infra/ with scripts/ and tailscale-state/.
2. In the Tailscale admin console, mint a reusable, tagged auth key (e.g. tag:bot-controller). Tagged nodes have no key expiry. If Tailnet Lock is on, pre-sign the key or sign the node once from a signing node; never put Lock signing keys on the Grok Bot computer.
3. Store the key as an injected secret TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY_SIGNED via the secure secret request. Never paste it into chat.
4. Start tailscaled with persistent state under that folder, then tailscale up with the auth key and advertise tags. If the node was already up with state elsewhere, stop it, copy that state into the folder, and restart so it keeps the same IP.
5. scripts/restore-tailscale.sh (idempotent, never echoes secrets): install Tailscale if missing; start tailscaled with persistent state if not running; fast path exit 0 if BackendState is Running and not locked out; else require TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY_SIGNED starting with tskey-auth- (exit 10 NEED_SECRET if absent) and run tailscale up; exit 20 NEED_LOCK_SIGNATURE if locked out.
6. scripts/detect-fresh-box.sh: exit 0 when restore is needed (binary missing, daemon down, backend not Running, or locked out).
7. Hourly, every-day routine: run detect; if needed, run restore and re-verify. Silent when healthy. Report RESTORED (with IP) or BLOCKED (NEED_SECRET means a secure secret request; NEED_LOCK_SIGNATURE means ask a signing node). No weekday-only schedules; updates happen on weekends too.

## Prove it (uninstall drill)
Run once after setup and after changes, at a quiet time:
1. Record tailscale ip -4.
2. Simulate an update (stop daemon + remove package).
3. Run detect (expect exit 0), then restore (expect exit 0).
4. Pass = same IP as step 1, lock status shows the node signed, and a known tailnet host answers.
5. Keep a manual fallback so a failed drill never leaves the bot offline.

## Fleet lessons
- Tailscale grants between tag:hermes-node hosts must include tcp:8642 if a fleet-health aggregator host probes the other nodes; otherwise the health guard shows false RED.
- After dismantling any direct mesh (Thunderbolt bridge or similar), audit for leftover bridge IPs in Hermes provider/peer URLs and tailscale serve targets.

## Recovery guidance
Recover a wedged computer with Update Grok Bot's Computer (keeps files and logins). Avoid Reset unless nothing else works; it restores an older snapshot.

## Done checklist
Every file under /home/box? Something automatic reinstalls/restarts it after an update? Drill passed? If any answer is no, say so plainly instead of calling it done.

skills.name: Tailscale fleet macOS
skills.description: Use when managing or recovering Tailscale fleet nodes (key expiry, Tailnet Lock, MagicDNS, ACL tags, system extension, greyed Remove in admin console, or Tailscale SSH between Hermes hosts).
skills.content:
---
name: Tailscale fleet macOS
description: >-
  Use when managing or recovering Tailscale fleet nodes (key expiry, Tailnet
  Lock, MagicDNS, ACL tags, system extension, greyed Remove in admin console, or
  Tailscale SSH between Hermes hosts).
---
# Tailscale macOS Fleet Operations

Manage, authenticate, configure, and recover Tailscale across a Hermes macOS fleet. The orchestrator bot is orchestrator-only — delegate node-side recovery to the designated recovery agent unless the Owner overrides.

## When to Use

Load this skill when the request or symptom touches ANY of: `tailscale` CLI, Tailscale admin console, Tailnet Lock, MagicDNS, fleet ACL tags, node key expiry, macOS system extension / network extension, or Tailscale SSH between fleet nodes. If the request only involves non-Tailscale networking (Cloudflare, NordVPN alone, LAN), skip this skill.

## Fleet Topology (SSOT — fill from Owner install)

| Node role | Placeholder | MagicDNS | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator + primary | `<NODE_ORCHESTRATOR>` | `<NODE_ORCHESTRATOR>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Coding limb | `<NODE_CODING>` | `<NODE_CODING>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Merge / coding seat | `<NODE_MERGE>` | `<NODE_MERGE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Inference limb | `<NODE_INFERENCE>` | `<NODE_INFERENCE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Workhorse | `<NODE_WORKHORSE>` | `<NODE_WORKHORSE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Controller (separate) | `<NODE_CONTROLLER>` | — | `<TAG_CONTROLLER>` |

MagicDNS domain: `*.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` — preferred host-to-host path. Prefer MagicDNS over raw IPs; IPs can shift after sleep/wake. Document whether Tailnet Lock is enabled and whether ACL is default-deny.

Authorized inter-tag traffic (example pattern): `<TAG_CONTROLLER>` → `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` over TCP ports used for SSH, Hermes HTTP API (`8642`), and any fleet health probe port the Owner defined.

## Variant Handling — Which CLI Do I Have?

Tailscale on macOS ships in three variants. NEVER run Standalone and App Store variants simultaneously.

**Detect first, always:**
```bash
ls /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale 2>/dev/null && echo "GUI_APP_PRESENT"
ls /usr/local/bin/tailscale /opt/homebrew/bin/tailscale 2>/dev/null
which tailscale
tailscale version 2>&1 | head -3
```

**Variant differences:**

| Variant | CLI path | System extension | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standalone | `/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale` | Yes (`tailscale configure sysext`) | Full feature set; preferred for fleet |
| Mac App Store | Same GUI path | Network Extension (NE) | Tailscale SSH is NOT available on App Store build — known blocker for artifact pushes over Tailscale SSH |
| Open-source `tailscaled` | `/usr/local/bin/tailscale` (utun) | None | Linux-style; CLI-only node |

**System extension control (Standalone only):**
```bash
tailscale configure sysext activate
tailscale configure sysext status
tailscale configure sysext deactivate
```

**App Store recovery:** if a node was installed from App Store and Tailscale SSH fails, the operator must reinstall via Standalone variant or use another path the Owner approved.

## Key Expiry Recovery — The Common Failure

Each Hermes node can have a node-key expiry date enforced by Tailnet Lock. When a node's key expires, that node goes RED — health checks time out, Hermes HTTP `:8642` unreachable, connectors fail with URLError.

### Recovery Flow

**Step 1 — Check state before doing anything:**
```bash
tailscale status
tailscale lock status 2>/dev/null   # only on signing-capable nodes
```

If the node is fully locked out and unreachable, the operator must extend the key from the [admin console](https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines) — find the device → ⋯ menu → "Temporarily extend key" → short window.

**Step 2 — Re-authenticate (NEVER over SSH/RDP without an alternate login path):**
```bash
sudo tailscale up --force-reauth
```

The new node key is often signed automatically using the node's Tailnet Lock key — manual re-signing is NOT required in normal cases.

**Step 3 — Verify as a signing node:**
```bash
tailscale lock status
```

If the recovered node's `tlpub:` is missing from the trusted list (rare — only if auto-rotation failed), re-add from another trusted signing node:
```bash
tailscale lock add tlpub:<recovered-node-key>
```

**Step 4 — Disable key expiry on signing nodes (PREVENTION):**
Signing nodes should have key expiry DISABLED. Do this from the admin console per node, or via ACL node attributes. Keep a fleet-health warning (e.g. 14-day expiry guard) until all signing nodes are no-expiry.

## Tailnet Lock — Signing-Node Invariants

- Signing nodes are a subset of Hermes nodes. Name primary and secondary signing nodes in the Owner's install notes.
- When a signing node's key expires and the user re-auths, the node's signature often rotates automatically. Do NOT manually `tailscale lock remove` unless explicitly directed by the Owner.
- Stale machine registrations must be DELETED from the Tailnet Lock admin list before that name can rejoin.
- To list current signing nodes: `tailscale lock status` from any trusted signing node.

## ACL Tags & Connectivity Rules

If the fleet ACL is default-deny, Hermes-node-to-hermes-node is NOT automatic — only the explicit controller → node rules the Owner defined are guaranteed.

**Diagnostic command when a node appears reachable (UDP) but TCP fails:**
```bash
tailscale ping <node-name-or-magicdns>
tailscale netcheck
```

`tailscale netcheck` reports path MTU, DERP relay, and which ports are blocked end-to-end. If `netcheck` shows fleet ports blackholed, suspect ACL — not the node itself.

## Fleet Health Probes

Maintain a key-expiry guard (e.g. page within 14 days of expiry). Keep a per-node health file under the Owner's fabric-health path — read it FIRST when investigating fleet RED states.

A node is RED when: ping fails AND Hermes `:8642` times out AND the health-probe port times out AND the Hermes connector errors. A node is GREEN when ping + required ports respond.

## MagicDNS Addressing Rules

- ALWAYS address fleet nodes by MagicDNS name (`<NODE>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>`), NEVER raw IPs when MagicDNS works.
- IPs are provisional — they can shift after sleep/wake, especially on WiFi.
- Treat any stored IP as suspect. If a node's stored IP differs from a fresh `tailscale status`, use the fresh one.
- The `100.100.x.x` range is Tailscale's CGNAT space (not a node) — that is the DERP relay path.

## Tailscale + NordVPN Coexistence

If NordVPN is active, it MUST connect BEFORE Tailscale — otherwise DNS or exit-node overrides break MagicDNS resolution. Verify with `tailscale dns status` after NordVPN connects.

## Standing Rules

- Never run Standalone and App Store variants on the same node — pick one, document it in the node's profile note.
- Never `sed` Tailscale config files — use a structured patch tool or `tailscale set` / admin console.
- Never paste OAuth codes or auth keys in chat — Tailscale auth keys come from the admin console or `tailscale up --authkey <key>` via a masked secret path.
- Don't claim recovery succeeded without reading `tailscale status` + `tailscale lock status` + a real ping.
- Don't `tailscale logout` a signing node without confirming a second signing node is still trusted — you can lock the fleet out of Tailnet Lock.
- Don't `tailscale down` on a node you SSH into without an alternate local console path.

## Quick Reference — Common Commands

```bash
# Identity & state
tailscale status
tailscale ping <node>
tailscale netcheck
tailscale version

# Auth
sudo tailscale up
sudo tailscale up --authkey <key>
sudo tailscale up --force-reauth

# Tailnet Lock
tailscale lock status
tailscale lock add tlpub:<key>
tailscale lock remove <node-key>   # Owner only

# System extension (Standalone only)
tailscale configure sysext activate
tailscale configure sysext status
tailscale configure sysext deactivate
```

## Admin console — Remove button greyed out

Docs do not spell out every UI reason the **Remove** control is disabled. Check these in order:

1. **Role.** Device removal needs **Owner**, **Admin**, or **IT admin**. Network admin, Billing admin, Auditor, and Member are read-only for devices ([roles](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/user-roles#roles); [remove a device](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/access-control/device-management/how-to/remove)).
2. **Shared-in node.** Devices shared into this tailnet from another account cannot be deleted with normal device-delete controls ([deleteDevice API](https://tailscale.com/api)).
3. **API delete (Owner / Admin / IT admin)** when the console stays stuck:
```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2/device/<deviceId>" \
  -u "<api-key>:"
```
Use a masked secret for the API key; never paste it in chat. Replace `<deviceId>` with the node id ([remove a device](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/access-control/device-management/how-to/remove)).
4. If role is correct, the device is not an external share, and console/API still block removal, escalate to [Tailscale Support](https://tailscale.com/contact/support).

## Escalation

When the orchestrator hits a Tailscale issue that requires node-side commands, logging into a console, or `sudo tailscale up --force-reauth`, delegate to the designated recovery agent with the fleet-health file path and the symptom. Only escalate to the Owner if an admin console action is required (key extension, ACL edit) or if the second signing node is also compromised.
